description: Authentication Spoofing via Cognito Identity Pool An attacker could obtain valid credentials through phishing, credential stuffing, or brute force attacks. Once authenticated, they receive temporary AWS credentials through the Identity Pool and can access resources based on the assigned IAM role. An attacker uses stolen researcher credentials to authenticate via Cognito, receives temporary AWS credentials, and gains access to sensitive patient data in S3.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1550 - Use Alternate Authentication Material
recommendation: Enhance Password Policy and Implement Advanced Security Features

description: Unauthorized Data Access via KMS Key Misuse Attackers could exploit overly permissive KMS key policies, IAM roles with unnecessary key permissions, or attempt to use cross-account key access if not properly restricted. An attacker compromises a service role with broad KMS permissions, uses it to decrypt sensitive data across multiple storage services, and exfiltrates the decrypted content.
references: recommendation: Implement Strict Key Policy Controls
recommendation: Implement Key Rotation and Access Reviews

description: Data Tampering During Transit Attackers could attempt man-in-the-middle attacks, exploit misconfigured TLS settings, or compromise network paths to intercept and modify data in transit. An attacker exploits a misconfigured VPC endpoint policy to intercept and modify patient data being uploaded to S3.

Compute Resource Denial of Service Attackers could submit excessive job requests, exploit resource allocation mechanisms, or target individual compute nodes with CPU/memory exhaustion attacks. An attacker submits numerous large batch jobs that consume all available compute resources, preventing legitimate jobs from processing.

recommendation: Implement Resource Quotas and Throttling

description: Side-Channel Attacks on HPC Cluster Attackers could exploit CPU cache timing, speculative execution vulnerabilities, or other hardware-level side channels to extract information from co-located instances. An attacker runs a malicious workload on the same physical host as a target EC2 instance and uses cache timing attacks to extract cryptographic keys.

ML Model and Training Data Exposure Attackers could exploit misconfigured SageMaker notebook instances, intercept model artifacts during training, or access training data through improperly secured storage. An attacker gains access to a SageMaker notebook instance and extracts sensitive training data or proprietary model parameters.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
mitreATT&CK: T1213 - Data from Information Repositories

description: Data Exfiltration via High-Performance Storage Attackers could exploit misconfigured mount targets, abuse file system permissions, or leverage compromised compute instances to exfiltrate data from high-performance storage. An attacker compromises an EC2 instance with access to FSx Lustre and uses high-bandwidth storage to quickly exfiltrate large amounts of data.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1048 - Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
